Howdy neighbor!
I should probably start by saying that typically to "qualify" for MAEAP FWH (Forest & Wetlands Habitat) verification there needs to be 10 acres, although I think they'll go as low as 5 in some cases. This is something that NRCS and DNR have some (albeit limited sometimes) funding to help offset costs for the development of these plans - although I will say this small of a footprint might not qualify for funding, and ultimately if you're not doing it for a MAEAP verification it's not entirely necessary, although it would help you to develop a plan to keep your forest healthy. Granted it might get very complicated with multiple property owners being involved as well.
Second, I want to give you a recommendation to reach out to Nathan Ayers. He is a part of the Agroforestry Coalition, and he would be a great resource to help you put a plan together for establishing this food forest. The first link will send you to the West MI Agroforestry Partnership, and if you click "forest farming" under "The 5 Agroforestry Systems," it will lead you to the second link that's listed, which is an informational page (on USDA / USFS website) that discusses Forest Farming and has several resources that you can look into if you're interested.

Thanks for reaching out Jim, and thanks for what you're doing! Sounds like a sweet project. I hope you have a great day!


Hey Jim!
Following up after our site visit on Friday last week. I have gotten in touch with some connections of mine and have received some helpful information.
First, I was informed that the federal funding that the state has available for developing FSP's (Forestry Stewardship Plans) is actually suspended for FY25 & likely FY 26 (Fiscal Year). So unless EQIP (Environmental Quality Incentives Program - housed within NRCS) supports/approves your FSP, you / your HOA would likely have to pay out of pocket to fund the development of your FSP.
I can connect you with our district conservationist, Matt Soehnel, to see if developing a FSP for this project might be eligible for partial funding through EQIP (Environmental Quality Incentives Program), or if this is something you would likely have to pay out of pocket to develop. I don't believe the funding through NRCS is frozen anymore, so hopefully this is a possibility for you. Granted, the application window may also come into play, and if it's closed, you'll have to submit an EQIP application for FY26 to receive any funding for the FSP.
I also included some examples and other helpful resources that were shared with me.
First, there's a list of required components for any FSP
Second is a document that offers guidance on the development of a FSP
Third is an example of a finished FSP
Fourth, there's a list of 8 different plan checklists that cover some of the different options / avenues for the development of a forestry stewardship/management plan.
Fifth is a recently completed FSP for Byron Center Christian Schools - this might be a little more extensive than what you're hoping to cover in your FSP, but it does discuss educational goals and benefits in the plan, which seems like something you may also include in your plan.
Let me know if you have any questions on this, and I will share your project with our district conservationist to see if he has any feedback or recommendations.
Be in touch and enjoy the rest of your day!

Jim,
I can absolutely relate, the density of these plans can definitely be a struggle. Even when you don't get 2 or 3 at once! I've sent an email to our District Conservationist (DC) asking whether this undertaking would be worthwhile, and am awaiting their response. Development of a FSP could very well be worthwhile (usually, the smaller the area, the smaller the plan, the less work is involved, and the more affordable the associated costs are), but whether you'd be eligible (with good odds) to have an EQIP (or other NRCS program) application accepted or approved could be an entirely different story. FSP's are often developed with intentions of applying for funding through conservation programs, but even if you didn't have a strong chance of being selected, this would offer you a comprehensive plan on how to approach proper management of your forestland. It could help estimate future costs, or even include a plan to improve your path to become stroller accessible for example. Not to mention then you could get MAEAP verified!
I don't want to get too far into the weeds here or tempt your wildest ambitions with this project, but I'll let you know what I hear back from our DC and we can go from there.
If I don't hear back before tomorrow, I hope you have a wonderful holiday weekend!
Best,
Michael Ewing
CTAP / MAEAP Technician
